sub.en: Look at the pairs. Does the word describe the THING, or the way somebody does something?

items.why: An adjective describes a thing or a person: a careful driver. An adverb describes an action: she drives carefully.
The adverb of good is well — never “goodly”.

items.q: Please talk ___ — we’re in a library.
This jacket is ___ comfortable. I love it.
It’s ___ expensive, but I’ll take it.
items.why: quite = a bit, but not completely. very = a lot.

use: Do you offer a student discount?
tts: Excuse me? — Yes? How can I help? — How much is this magazine? — It’s four pounds ninety-nine.
Right, and do you offer a student discount? — Yes, we do. You get twenty per cent off.
Oh, that’s good. Do you sell batteries? — Yes, we do. What kind do you need? — AA, please. Just one packet.
Can I help you? — No, thanks. I’m just looking. — Well, if you need anything, just ask. — Can I try this hoodie on, please? — Yes, of course. The changing rooms are over there.

acts.title: Three reviews
text: ★★★★★ “These boots are really comfortable and they fit perfectly. I walk about eight kilometres a day and my feet don’t hurt. They aren’t cheap, but they’re good value for money.”
★★☆☆☆ “The jacket looks good in the photo, but the size is wrong. I ordered a medium and it arrived quite small. I’m sending it back. The shop answered my email very quickly, though.”
★★★☆☆ “Useful bag, badly made. It carries everything, but after two months one handle is broken. Buy it if you need it now; don’t buy it for five years.”

write.q: Write a shop conversation and a short review: 4 lines in the shop (ask the price, ask to try it on, ask about the size, ask about a discount) and 2 lines of review with one adjective and one adverb.
write.model: Excuse me, how much is this jacket? Can I try it on, please? Have you got it in a bigger size? Do you offer a student discount? — REVIEW: It’s a really comfortable jacket and it fits perfectly. The shop answered my email very quickly, so I’ll buy there again.

speak.q: Play both parts out loud: as the customer ask four questions, and as the assistant give four replies. Then describe one thing you own with an adjective and one adverb.
speak.model: How much is this? — It’s 4,000 tenge. Can I try it on? — Of course, the changing rooms are over there. — My boots are really comfortable and they were made well.
